title: lets-make-the-hardcoded-workflow-dynamically-loa
description: lets make the hardcoded workflow dynamically loadable so it is possible to define multiple workflows and specify which one to use, if none is provided it defaults to the current one

researchNotes: Changeflow implementation is concentrated in `pi/extensions/changeflow/index.ts`. The workflow *definition* is currently a module-level `machineDefinition` constant with a fixed `WorkflowState` union, `workflowStateList`, a single module-level `changeflowMachine = createMachine(machineDefinition)`, and helper functions (`canonicalStateConfig`, `stateMeta`, `statesMatchingMeta`, `toWorkflowState`, `initialWorkflowSnapshot`, `applyTransition`, `saveWorkflow`) that all assume that one canonical definition. Workflow instances persist `machineDefinition` and `machineSnapshot` in `.pi/changeflow/<id>/workflow.json`, but runtime helpers ignore the persisted definition and use the hardcoded constant.

The current default lifecycle and phase behavior are already mostly serializable/config-driven: `machineDefinition.states.*.meta.changeflow` carries `autoContinue`, `editPolicy`, `prompt.instructions`, review/submission/plannotator mappings, execution-order metadata, and subagent role permissions/overrides. This makes the existing `machineDefinition` a good candidate to move into a workflow-definition module/file and keep as the default workflow.

Current user-facing workflow selection has no support: `/changeflow start <description>` treats everything after `start` as the description, creates an ID from it, sets `state: "research"`, calls `initialWorkflowSnapshot()` for the single machine, and queues the research prompt. `status`, `advance`, tool handlers, prompt injection, review reconciliation, edit blocking, and subagent validation all operate on one `activeWorkflow` instance and the single hardcoded definition.

Pi extension docs confirm this extension style can be modular and async: directory extensions can import helper modules; TypeScript is loaded by jiti; the default export can be async before startup; npm dependencies and Node fs/path are available. So dynamic workflow discovery can be implemented inside this extension by loading built-in/project-local workflow definition modules or JSON at extension startup, while keeping `/reload` compatibility.

Likely implementation shape: introduce a `WorkflowDefinition` abstraction containing `id`/`name`, XState machine config, initial event (currently START), optional artifact templates (currently research.md/high-level-plan.md), and possibly default selection metadata. Create a registry/loader that registers the current `changeflow.mvp` definition as the default and can discover additional definitions. Persist the selected definition ID on each workflow instance so restore/advance/review/tool handlers can resolve the correct machine and metadata instead of using module-level `changeflowMachine`.

Type risk: supporting genuinely different state machines means `WorkflowState` cannot remain a closed union of the current state names. Helpers should move toward `type WorkflowState = string` (or a branded string) plus runtime validation from each definition's `states`; `workflowStateList` should be derived from `Object.keys(definition.machineConfig.states)`. Existing tool logic can remain metadata-driven using state meta rather than hardcoded state names. Review kind/subagent role unions can stay constrained.

Selection UX options found in current command parser: because `/changeflow start` currently does simple whitespace splitting, adding an option like `/changeflow start --workflow <id> <description>` or `/changeflow start <workflowId> -- <description>` requires a small parser. Default behavior should preserve `/changeflow start <description>` using the current MVP workflow. A `/changeflow workflows` or status output could list known workflow definition IDs for discoverability.

Files likely to change: `pi/extensions/changeflow/index.ts` for definition resolution, workflow persistence schema, command parsing, and helper refactors; a new `pi/extensions/changeflow/workflows/` module or `workflow-definitions.ts` to hold the current default definition and registry; `pi/extensions/changeflow/README.md` to document defining/selecting workflows. `subagents.ts` probably does not need changes unless workflow definitions also customize the global role catalog.

Validation available: `cd pi/extensions/changeflow && npm run check` runs TypeScript noEmit. There are no existing tests in the package, so QA should include typecheck plus manual/inspection checks: default `/changeflow start <description>` still selects current workflow, explicit workflow selection persists `definitionId`, restore resolves the right definition, invalid workflow IDs fail clearly, and transitions/submission/review/subagent/edit-policy helpers read metadata from the selected definition.
decisions: Research complete: identified the hardcoded single-machine assumptions, current metadata-driven default definition, likely workflow-definition registry/loader shape, selection UX points, type risks for multiple state sets, files to change, and validation approach.

Implemented dynamically loadable workflow definitions: added `workflows.ts` with XState-typed `ChangeflowWorkflowDefinition`, built-in default `changeflow.mvp`, JSON loading from `.pi/changeflow/workflows/*.json`, registry validation, per-workflow `workflowDefinitionId` persistence/default fallback, definition-aware transition/meta helpers, `/changeflow start --workflow <id>`, `/changeflow workflows`, status definition display, and artifact templates. Updated README and tsconfig. Validation passed with `cd pi/extensions/changeflow && npm run check`.
Implementation complete and typecheck passed (`cd pi/extensions/changeflow && npm run check`).

QA validation passed: reran `cd pi/extensions/changeflow && npm run check` successfully. Inspected references confirming `workflowDefinitionId` persistence/default fallback, registry/default ID, workflow selection parser, `/changeflow workflows`, tsconfig inclusion, and README documentation are present.
QA complete: TypeScript check passed and implementation/docs were inspected for the dynamic workflow definition paths.

User validation rejected: default workflow should not be embedded in registry source; it should live in its own bundled TypeScript workflow file and be loaded like user-provided workflows, with only default selection being special.

Addressed user validation feedback: moved the bundled default `changeflow.mvp` workflow definition out of `workflows.ts` into its own TypeScript workflow file at `pi/extensions/changeflow/bundled-workflows/changeflow-mvp.ts`. `workflows.ts` now only imports/registers it through the registry; the definition data (phase instructions, machine config, artifact templates) is no longer embedded in the registry module. Updated tsconfig and README. Validation passed with `cd pi/extensions/changeflow && npm run check`.
QA complete after addressing validation feedback: default workflow is now in its own bundled TypeScript workflow file and typecheck passes.

reviews.feedback:
# Plan Feedback

I've reviewed this plan and have 1 piece of feedback:

## 1. (line 12) Feedback on: "Define types such as:
WorkflowState = string
WorkflowMachineConfig = { id: string; initial: string; states: Record<string, ChangeflowStateConfig> }
ChangeflowWorkflowDefinition = { id: string; title/name?: string; description?: string; initialEvent?: string; machineDefinition: WorkflowMachineConfig; artifactTemplates?: ... }"
> We should type the workflow as an xstate config, not re-create similiar types ourselves
